summary: BLAgent localizes the faulty file for a SWE-bench-Lite bug report by embedding path-prefixed AST chunks, rewriting the report into a structural query and a behavioral query, and reranking at most 15 files with a bounded ReAct pass plus one evidence-anchored prompt. On 300 Python issues it reports Top-1 of 78.6% with GPT-OSS-120B and 86.7% with Claude 4.6 Sonnet, at about $0.09 per Claude instance, and a best-of-three Agentless repair gain when its files replace Agentless localization.

claims.claim: BLAgent reaches Top-1 78.6% (MRR 0.851) with an open model and 86.7% (MRR 0.900) with Claude 4.6 Sonnet, above published file-level localizers
claims.evidence: Table 1(a): GPT-OSS BLAgent Top-1 0.786 versus reproduced Agentless GPT-OSS 0.623 and published LocAgent Claude-3.5 0.777, OpenHands Claude-3.5 0.762, LocAgent Qwen-2.5-32B fine-tuned 0.759. Most of those baselines are different models and, for AutoCodeRover and OpenHands, numbers copied from other papers. Table 1(b): same-model Claude 4.6 comparison is BLAgent 0.867 on all 300 versus LocAgent 0.824 on the 182 instances a $300 budget finished; on that subset the authors report BLAgent Top-1 0.906. Localization temperature is 0.7 and threats to validity say localization runs were not repeated.

claims.claim: Path-augmented AST chunking and dual query rewriting improve retrieval, and bounded agentic reranking improves on one-shot RAG
claims.evidence: Table 3 dense MRR: text 0.459, AST 0.473, AST plus path 0.553 (relative +20.4% vs text, +16.9% vs AST). AST alone is a small step. Table 5: structural rewrite lifts dense MRR from 0.553 to 0.680; both rewrites lift Phase-1 BLAgent only from 0.769 to 0.795. Table 4: basic RAG Top-1 0.673, Phase 1 0.685, Phase 2 0.762. At Top-10, path-aware dense retrieval (0.873) beats LLM reranking (0.823).

claims.claim: BLAgent is more than 18 times cheaper than LocAgent under the same Claude model
claims.evidence: §5.1, Table 11: Claude BLAgent is 26,180 prompt plus 582 completion tokens, $0.09 per instance, $27 for 300. LocAgent on a $300 cap finished 158 of 182 attempted instances at $0.89 each on the successes and $1.65 if the whole $300 is divided by 182, which is the 18x figure. The ratio counts LocAgent timeouts and 800k-token loops. A completed-only ratio is about 10x.

claims.claim: Swapping BLAgent into Agentless raises end-to-end repair by up to 25%
claims.evidence: Table 9 reports the best of three runs, not the mean: regression-test setting 108/300 (36.0%) versus native 86/300 (28.6%), relative +25.5%; majority vote 102 vs 83 (+22.8%); reproduction tests 115 vs 96 (+19.7%). A paired Wilcoxon on per-bug solve counts across the three runs gives p=0.014. Empty patches fall from 38 to 14. Resolution stays near 38% despite ~80% Top-1 file accuracy. Twenty-three matplotlib issues could not run the newer tests.

patterns.note: File-level bug localization is treated as repository exploration. Against a re-run Agentless localizer on the same GPT-OSS model, Top-1 moves from 0.623 to 0.786 (Table 1). The same-model LocAgent comparison also favors BLAgent but only on the 182 instances LocAgent finished. Open repository traversal is not the winner here: the agent never sees files outside a retrieval top-15, and every Claude failure the authors inspected was a retrieval miss (14 cases, §3.2.3).

Table 3 isolates chunk text. Prepending the relative path to AST chunks raises dense MRR from 0.473 to 0.553 and Top-10 from 0.703 to 0.873. Table 5 isolates the query: a structural rewrite raises dense MRR from 0.553 to 0.680. One-shot LLM reranking then helps Top-1 and hurts Top-10 (0.823 vs 0.873).

Phase-1 skeleton ReAct plus Phase-2 evidence prompt beat one-shot RAG on the same candidates (Table 4, Top-1 0.762 vs 0.673). Table 12 shows giving that second stage 10 files or 10 chunks instead of 5 does not raise Top-1. The loop is bounded; this is not evidence for open-ended exploration.
AST structure is used only to cut chunks. Versus fixed-size text, AST chunking alone moves dense MRR from 0.459 to 0.473 (Table 3). The paper does not compare grep, BM25, or an LSP.

methodology.sample: SWE-bench-Lite, 300 Python issues from a handful of repositories (django 114 and sympy 77 are cited in the failure analysis). Repair uses the same 300 inside Agentless, top-3 files, 40 patches at temperature 0.8.
methodology.baselines: Published SWE-bench-Lite file-localization numbers at each system's best reported model, plus Agentless re-run with GPT-OSS, plus LocAgent re-run with Claude 4.6 on a $300 budget (182/300). Chunking, query, phase, and context-size ablations use the authors' own pipeline.
methodology.models: GPT-OSS-120B via Ollama as the main agent; Claude 4.6 Sonnet; Qwen3-32B in the backbone table. Embeddings: nomic-embed-text-v1. Repair model is GPT-OSS-120B.
methodology.variance: Localization is a single temperature-0.7 pass; §7 says repeated localization trials were not done. Repair is three runs; the headline table is the best run, with a Wilcoxon on the three.
methodology.ablations: Chunking (Table 3), RAG versus two-phase rerank (Table 4), query transforms and order (Tables 5–6), model scale (Table 7), files and chunks in Phase 2 (Table 12).
methodology.contamination_controls: Pre-fix commits are used. No decontamination for SWE-bench issues that public models may have seen. LocAgent's paper drops some no-function-edit instances that BLAgent counts as failures.
methodology.languages: Python only. Prompts say 'Python bug reports'. Java Defects4J is discussed as prior work and not evaluated.

standards.peer_review: Accepted to ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM), arXiv v2, 18 May 2026. journal_ref not yet filled.

biases.detail: The leaderboard mixes GPT-OSS BLAgent with Claude-3.5 and GPT-4o systems, and with numbers taken from other papers. The matched Claude comparison covers 182 of 300 instances because LocAgent blew the budget.
SWE-bench-Lite is Python. Ten of 14 retrieval failures are sympy, where the report vocabulary does not match the edited file.
Public GitHub issues and fixes are the benchmark. No contamination audit.
File-level Top-1 is one stochastic pass at temperature 0.7. Repair variance exists but Table 9 prints the best of three.
The 18x cost ratio uses LocAgent's failed and truncated runs in the denominator. Completed runs are closer to 10x.
All headline numbers are SWE-bench-Lite. The threats section says industrial repositories and non-Python code are untested.
About 80% Top-1 file accuracy becomes about 38% resolved issues. File rank is not repair success, which the authors note and the abstract still pairs as a 25% repair gain.

coi.affiliations: University of Calgary and York University
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Claude 4.6 Sonnet is a third-party API. GPT-OSS is an open weight. No author product.
coi.detail: Academic paper accepted at TOSEM. No vendor affiliation.

verdict_reason: The within-pipeline ablations are the load-bearing evidence: path prefixes and a structural query move dense retrieval a lot, a second bounded rerank moves Top-1 further, and swapping the file list into Agentless raises resolved bugs on three runs (p=0.014). The 86.7% and 18x headlines lean on unmatched or budget-truncated baselines, localization itself was not repeated, and the benchmark is Python SWE-bench-Lite.
applicability: For issue triage across the the repositories, retrieve a small candidate set before any agent walks the tree, and put the file path in the indexed text. A structural query (exception, class, module) helps the first hop more than a symptom paraphrase. Cap the agent at the retrieved files; BLAgent's remaining misses were files the retriever never returned, several of them a dependency of the crash site rather than the crash site itself. Do not expect file-level accuracy to become a merged fix: even at ~80% Top-1 the repair rate stayed near 38%. Re-measure on Java. SWE-bench-Lite will not stand in for Spring services split across repositories, and this pipeline does not answer architecture or onboarding questions.

conflicts_with.detail: That review finds LLM re-ranking the largest localization gain, measured mostly against a weak path-embedding first stage at Hit@5. BLAgent's Table 3 shows the opposite at Top-10 once chunks already carry paths: dense retrieval 0.873 versus LLM rerank 0.823. The two can sit together if reranking helps only when the first stage is weak, which is the caveat already in the 2607.11046 review.
